{{Short description|Category where each homset contains at most one morphism}}
In [[mathematics]], specifically [[category theory]], a '''thin category''',<ref>{{nlab|id=thin+category|title=Thin category}}</ref> or '''posetal category''',{{Citation needed|reason=The term "posetal category" is not commonly used, and it's unclear whether it means the same thing as "thin category" or "poset seen as category" (skeletal thin category).|date=May 2026}} is a [[Category (mathematics)|category]] whose [[Category (mathematics)#Small and large categories|homsets]] each contain at most one morphism.<ref>{{Cite book |last=Roman |first=Steven |url={{Google books|y3LbDQAAQBAJ|page=5|plainurl=yes}}} |title=An Introduction to the Language of Category Theory |date=2017 |publisher=Springer International Publishing |isbn=978-3-319-41916-9 |series=Compact Textbooks in Mathematics |location=Cham |pages=5 |doi=10.1007/978-3-319-41917-6}}</ref> As such, a thin category amounts to a [[preordered class]] (or a [[preordered set]], if its objects form a [[Set (mathematics)|set]]).<ref name="Mac Lane">{{cite book |first=Saunders |last=Mac Lane |author-link=Saunders Mac Lane |title=Categories for the working mathematician |language=en |edition=2 |series=Graduate Texts in Mathematics |volume=5 |publisher=Springer |location=New York, NY |date=1998 |isbn=978-0-387-98403-2 |issn=0072-5285 |doi=10.1007/978-1-4757-4721-8 |mr=1712872 |zbl=0906.18001}}, p. 11</ref>{{rp|}} A thin category that is [[skeletal category|skeletal]] (i.e. whose isomorphisms are endomorphisms) amounts to a [[partially ordered class]] (or a [[poset]] if the category is [[small category|small]]). A thin category is sometimes assumed skeletal.

Equivalently, a thin category is a category [[enriched category|enriched]] over the initial boolean algebra <math>2=\{0,1\}</math> regarded as a [[cartesian monoidal category]].

All [[diagram (category theory)|diagram]]s [[commutative diagram|commute]] in a thin category. When the commutative diagrams of a category are interpreted as a typed equational theory whose objects are the types, a [[indiscrete category|codiscrete]] thin category corresponds to an inconsistent theory understood as one satisfying the axiom ''x'' = ''y'' at all types.

Viewing a [[2-category]] as an [[enriched category]] whose hom-objects are categories, the hom-objects of any extension of a thin category to a [[2-category]] having the same 1-cells are [[monoid]]s.

Some [[Lattice (order)|lattice-theoretic]] structures are definable as (usually skeletal) thin categories of a certain kind. For example, under this assumption, a poset may be defined as a small skeletal thin category, a [[distributive lattice]] as a small skeletal thin [[distributive category]], a [[Heyting algebra]] as a small skeletal thin finitely [[cocomplete]] [[cartesian closed category]], and a [[Boolean algebra]] as a small skeletal thin finitely cocomplete [[*-autonomous category]]. Conversely, categories, distributive categories, finitely cocomplete cartesian closed categories, and finitely cocomplete *-autonomous categories can be considered the respective [[categorification]]s of posets, distributive lattices, Heyting algebras, and Boolean algebras.
